title: Five-year Local Option Levy for Police, Fire & 911 Operations.
ballot_label: Caption: Five-year Local Option Levy for Police, Fire & 911 Operations. Question: Shall Troutdale adopt a local option levy at $1.60 per $1,000 of assessed value for police, fire & 911 services? This measure may cause property taxes to increase more than three percent.
summary: Troutdale contracts for police, fire and 911 services. This five-year local option levy of $1.60 per $1,000 of assessed value would fund only police, fire and 911 operations, and the Council would replace the current $25 Public Safety Fee. The City says costs are rising faster than available funding and projects a $3 million gap next year growing to over $5 million by 2030.
yes_means: A yes vote approves a five-year Troutdale local option property tax levy of $1.60 per $1,000 of assessed value for police, fire and 911 services.
no_means: A no vote rejects the proposed five-year levy for police, fire and 911 services.
fiscal_impact: Per the ballot summary: estimated collections $3,556,392 (2027-28), $3,663,084 (2028-29), $3,772,977 (2029-30), $3,886,166 (2030-31) and $4,002,751 (2031-32). An average Troutdale home assessed at about $267,800 would pay about $428.48 a year; because the current Public Safety Utility Fee (about $300 a year) would be eliminated, the summary estimates a net annual increase of about $128.48.

arguments.author: Eric Anderson, former Troutdale City Councilor
arguments.statement: Former Troutdale City Councilor Eric Anderson argues the five-year levy is a temporary measure and that the City should finish its service-agreement restructuring before asking taxpayers for more.
arguments.excerpt: A temporary tax does not fix the underlying cost structure; it buys five years while taxpayers pay more.
